Close-spaced sublimation (CSS) technique was employed to perovskite crystallization using fully ambient condition (in terms of both atmosphere and pressure) vapor-assisted solution processing method (AC-VASP) 1, 6-7 . Therefore, PbI2 coated substrates were placed backward at a close distance (~ 2 mm) right above MAI powder in order to decrease the diffusion distance from MAI vapor to PbI2 film and heated at 150 °C for 120 min in a simple laboratory oven. After cooling down to room temperature, the perovskite surface was rinsed by anhydrous isopropyl alcohol to remove excess MAI supply.

The perovskite crystallization process was finalized with post-annealing step at 145 °C for 30 min in air. Then, after cooling to room temperature, for standard structured PSCs, the hole transporting material (HTM) of Spiro-OMeTAD was spin-coated on perovskite film with a speed of 4000 rpm for 30 s and ramp rate of 4000 rpm s -1 . The fluorine-doped tin oxide (FTO) transparent conductive glass substrates (15 Ω sq -1 , Solaronix) were ultrasonically washed with detergent deionized water, acetone, and ethanol in sequential steps for about 20 min, respectively. The cleaned FTO substrates were directly used for next procedure with no additional UV-Ozone or Oxygen plasma cleaning treatment. A mildly acidic solution of Titanium(IV) tetra isopropoxide (TTIP; ≥ 98%) in ethanol 4 was coated on the pre-cleaned FTO by spin-casting with a speed of 2000 rpm for 30 s and a ramp rate of 2000 rpm s -1 that was then annealed at 500 °C for 1h in air to prepare blocking layer of compact TiO2 (cTiO2).

A mesoporous TiO2 (mp- TiO2) layer was spin-coated with a speed of 5000 rpm for 30 s and a ramp rate of 5000 rpm s -1 , using homemade TiO2 paste 3 that was diluted in anhydrous ethanol with the mass ratio of 2:7, dried at 125 °C for 15 min, and then sintered at 500 °C for 1 h in air. For ZnAl-MMOs modified cell (ZnAl-MMOs/mp- TiO2), the mp-TiO2 substrate was first immersed in the ZnAl-LDH formamide-based colloidal suspension (1g L -1 ). Afterwards, a suitable amount of PbI2 (99.999% pure) solution (1.0 M) in ultra-dry DMF (≥ 99.9%) was spin-casted at 6500 rpm for 10 s on bare mp-TiO2 and ZnAl-MMOs/mp-TiO2 substrates and followed by annealing at 70 °C for 30 min.

Therefore, PbI2 coated substrates were placed backward at a close distance (~ 2 mm) right above MAI powder in order to decrease the diffusion distance from MAI vapor to PbI2 film and heated at 150 °C for 120 min in a simple laboratory oven. evidence.quote: To have a similar condition of heat treatment on all substrates, and to eliminate probable effects of formamide solvent on control devices as well, some of the bare mp-TiO2 substrates were immersed and treated in pure formamide solvent and all devices (immersed and non-immersed substrates) experienced additional heat treatment at 500 °C for 1 h in air (control device). Afterwards, a suitable amount of PbI2 (99.999% pure) solution (1.0 M) in ultra-dry DMF (≥ 99.9%) was spin-casted at 6500 rpm for 10 s on bare mp-TiO2 and ZnAl-MMOs/mp-TiO2 substrates and followed by annealing at 70 °C for 30 min.

The temperatures of both the PbI 2 solution and substrates were fixed at 70 °C before deposition 5 . Close-spaced sublimation (CSS) technique was employed to perovskite crystallization using fully ambient condition (in terms of both atmosphere and pressure) vapor-assisted solution processing method (AC-VASP) 1, 6-7 . Therefore, PbI2 coated substrates were placed backward at a close distance (~ 2 mm) right above MAI powder in order to decrease the diffusion distance from MAI vapor to PbI2 film and heated at 150 °C for 120 min in a simple laboratory oven. After cooling down to room temperature, the perovskite surface was rinsed by anhydrous isopropyl alcohol to remove excess MAI supply.

evidence.quote: The perovskite crystallization process was finalized with post-annealing step at 145 °C for 30 min in air. Then, after cooling to room temperature, for standard structured PSCs, the hole transporting material (HTM) of Spiro-OMeTAD was spin-coated on perovskite film with a speed of 4000 rpm for 30 s and ramp rate of 4000 rpm s -1 . unresolved_notes: The source states that some bare mp-TiO2 substrates were immersed and treated in pure formamide solvent, while immersed and non-immersed control substrates all received the additional heat treatment. It does not identify which reported control devices or populations received the formamide treatment, so that group-only distinction was not assigned to an individual device.

The stability specimens are explicitly described as best-performing control and modified PSCs, but the source does not explicitly establish that they are physically identical to Cell No. 11 and Cell No. 8 in the batch tables. They are therefore retained as separate individual devices.

The IPCE and Mott-Schottky outcomes are attributed to complete device designs, but the physical identities of the measured cells are not reported. Separate measurement-specific devices were created rather than linking these results to batch-table cells.

Forward and reverse J-V curves are mentioned for control and modified standard PSCs, but the supplied passages contain no usable forward-scan numerical outcome. No forward-scan performance observation was created.

The reported 36.4% modified-PSC performance improvement is a design-level comparison rather than an individual-device outcome or a population statistic. The present schema has no family-level generic property field, so it is not reassigned to a specimen.
Only table rows present in the supplied evidence were extracted as individual devices. Missing rows from the twenty-device and five-device tables were not reconstructed.

The source reports maximum efficiencies of 18.54% for the modified standard PSC and 14.45% for the modified HTM-free PSC; these values uniquely match Cell No. 8 and Cell No. 2, respectively, in the supplied tables, so those two table devices are marked as champions. No equivalent explicit maximum statement supports champion status for the control table devices.

The fabrication passage reports an active area of 0.09 cm 2 for the shadow-mask-defined gold electrode, whereas the batch and stability passages report a 0.09 cm 2 aperture area. These distinct source terms were preserved rather than treated as interchangeable.
